sources: Live SDK docs at https://sdk.chain.wtf/ (casino/CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES, CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS, SLOTS_RISK_AND_RESERVES, VISUAL_AND_UX, RANDOMNESS_DICE, REPO_STRUCTURE, GETTING_STARTED, LOCAL_SIMULATOR, CHANGELOG) -- fetched and cross-checked 2026-09-28. This is treated as authoritative; CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md explicitly labels itself canonical/self-contained.

Superseded: the local casino-games-docs bundle (pixel-spin-onchain/SDK Standard) and chain-contracts-main's checked-in ICasinoGameV2.sol, both confirmed stale relative to the live docs as of the dates above.
_notes.interface_version_drift_resolved: Resolved 2026-09-28 against the live docs site: happydaze's ICasinoGameV2.sol shape (no `outcome` field on StepResult, has both quoteRiskParams and quoteForfeitPayout) IS the current canonical interface -- confirmed by the 'full Solidity'/'canonical' code block in CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md section 2.1. The only real drift was quoteRiskParams's 4th return value: renamed subJackpotVarianceScaled -> bodyVarianceScaled with a genuine semantics change (see quoteRiskParams rules below), not just a cosmetic rename. rubric/ICasinoGameV2.sol has been updated accordingly.
_notes.doc_internal_inconsistency_noted: CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md's prose (its own 'Game interface' bullet list) says StepResult includes an `outcome` field; the canonical Solidity code block in CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md section 2.1 does not have one. Per CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md's own disclaimer ('treat source files as authoritative if this doc drifts') and CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md's self-declared canonical status, the no-`outcome` shape is treated as correct.
_notes.pipeline_limitation_noted: LOCAL_SIMULATOR.md states its minimal casino stand-in runs with no diamond, no whitelist governance, and no portfolio risk accounting -- so the heavy-tail sigma-floor hard-revert (see quoteRiskParams/heavy-tail rules) is invisible to local simulator testing and can only be checked here, statically/via AI review, not inferred from 'it played fine in the simulator'. See SEM-17.

rules.description: Contract(s) compile cleanly under solc ^0.8.30 via forge build.

Contract implements all required ICasinoGameV2 functions with matching selectors (per rubric/ICasinoGameV2.sol). The quoteRiskParams 4th-return rename (subJackpotVarianceScaled -> bodyVarianceScaled) does not affect this check -- selectors are computed from input types only.
quoteCaps, quoteRiskParams, onSessionStart, onPlayerAction, onRandomness, quoteForfeitPayout are all declared view or pure (no state mutation) -- checked via ABI stateMutability.

Guest/host code never manually decodes the facet's encodedSession bytes via hardcoded byte offsets or a fixed total length (it grew 235->255 bytes when an operator address field was inserted, per the SDK changelog, so hardcoded-offset decoding silently breaks on protocol upgrades). Treat session bytes as opaque, or use the SDK's own codec. Also flag any game contract that tries to read/decode an operator address out of SessionContext -- games never see that field.
No selfdestruct usage.
No delegatecall usage.
No tx.origin usage (phishing/auth bypass vector).

Low-level value-call patterns (.call{value:) flagged. Since game step handlers are only ever reached via the facet's staticcall (CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md, Reentrancy), a `view`-declared ICasinoGameV2 method containing a value-transferring call is structurally either dead code or a bypass attempt -- treat any hit here as suspicious, not just informational.
block.timestamp / blockhash / block.prevrandao / block.difficulty not used as a randomness source -- randomness must come only from the onRandomness callback parameter.
Inline assembly blocks flagged for manual/AI review.
forge lint (high/medium severity) findings surfaced directly.
No use of a stale `probabilityBps` field name -- the live interface uses `probabilityWad` throughout (confirmed in CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md, SLOTS_RISK_AND_RESERVES.md, CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md).

Flag any raw small-modulus operation applied directly to a byte/nibble extracted from randomness/bytes32 (e.g. `% 6`, `(randomness[i] % 6) + 1`) with no preceding rejection/threshold comparison (e.g. `< 252`). This is a static hint for SEM-13 (the real unbiased-d6 MUST-requirement, RANDOMNESS_DICE.md) -- flag for confirmation, don't hard-fail on the grep alone.
game.manifest.json exists at the guest's own origin/root.
schemaVersion == 1.
gameId is a non-empty string.
apiVersion == 1.
defaultLocale is non-empty and present in locales with a non-empty name.
presentation.mode is 'full-iframe' or 'embedded'.
presentation.hostPanels.{openSession,history,status} are booleans.
capabilities.{openSession,submitAction,forfeitExpiredSession,cancelStuckRandomness,resize} are all booleans present, and capabilities.openSession === true for a betting game.

gameId's canonical form (strip trailing 'Game', lowercase, strip non-alphanumerics) is plausible given the contract name -- informational, real check happens at whitelist/registration time. Confirmed byte-for-byte against the live validateCasinoGameManifest/canonicalCasinoGameId source in CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md section 5.1.

Guest code never signs or broadcasts a transaction and never connects a wallet directly (no ethers.Wallet/signTransaction/sendTransaction/window.ethereum.request signing calls) -- it must only call hostApi.openSession/submitAction/cancelStuckRandomness/revealOutcome (the last is now a mandatory, non-signing call -- see UI-06).

postMessage/Penpal allowedOrigins does not silently resolve to '*' in a way that looks production-bound. getAllowedParentOrigins() falls back to ['*'] when document.referrer isn't parseable (CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md section 3.2); explicitly flagged dev-only in that doc's own security notes (section 8.2) -- production games should be served from a stable origin behind HTTPS.
Guest code visibly uses the SDK bridge pattern (connectGameToHost / Penpal WindowMessenger) rather than a custom/ad-hoc protocol.
npm audit high/critical advisories in guest dependencies.
ESLint / tsc pass, if a config is present (best-effort, non-blocking if absent).

Guest code calls hostApi.revealOutcome({ sessionId }) somewhere. This became a mandatory part of the guest contract (SDK changelog, marked Breaking): a game that never calls it after a win leaves the host's balance-display guard stale until the player reloads. Its absence entirely is a static red flag; whether it's called on every win path (not just eagerly, and not on the simplest spin only) needs the AI review -- see SEM-15.

If manifest.capabilities.resize === true, guest code calls observeGameContentSize(hostApi) or otherwise drives hostApi.reportContentSize({ minHeight }) once the bridge connects. This replaced the old static manifest field presentation.minHeight, which was removed from validation entirely (SDK changelog: 'height is now a runtime concern reported by the child iframe when capabilities.resize is supported') -- do not flag a missing static minHeight field, that's expected now.

Guest visibly respects ui.theme ('light'|'dark'|'system', including prefers-color-scheme when 'system') and ui.locale from the host-pushed snapshot, and applies prefers-reduced-motion to heavy slot/animation sequences (VISUAL_AND_UX.md). Informational, non-blocking.

gameData is decoded identically (same paytable/variant) across quoteCaps, quoteRiskParams, and onSessionStart/onRandomness. For multi-variant games, maxPayout/probabilityWad/expectedPayout/bodyVarianceScaled must all be recomputed from the same tables per variant (SLOTS_RISK_AND_RESERVES.md), not shared/stale constants.
onPlayerAction correctly reverts for instant/single-step games with no legitimate mid-round action, or correctly validates/handles actions for multi-step games.

The on-chain-enforced bound is `payout <= escrowedStake + reservedProfit` after each step's deltas (CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md, Payout cap), not directly quoteRiskParams.maxPayout -- the two should agree but are checked separately, and a mismatch reverts with CasinoGameFacet__InvalidPayout. Specifically check for two documented failure patterns: (a) 'reserve and payout must agree to the wei' -- quoteCaps/quoteRiskParams/onSessionStart/onRandomness should route through one shared payout function so rounding never pushes payout one base unit over budget; (b) 'don't release reserved profit on the settling step' -- a nonzero negative reservedProfitDelta/escrowDelta on the terminal step lowers the cap before the check runs, making every win above 1x revert.
probabilityWad is the probability of the top-tier/jackpot outcome specifically (not 'any win' or an average), is <= 1e18, and is internally consistent with the contract's own odds table.
expectedPayout matches the RTP actually implied by the paytable/weights used in onRandomness (no drift between quoted and simulated RTP).
Session phase-machine transitions (nextPhase / requestRandomnessNow) are correct for the game's step pattern and cannot be driven into an invalid or permanently stuck state.

UI never independently computes or lets the player submit a payout figure that isn't sourced from host-pushed on-chain state (gameState/balances are hints only; facet + game contract are authoritative -- CHAIN_WTF_CASINO_GAMES.md section 8.2, 'never trust client-only math for payouts').

General security review: backdoors/owner bypass, hardcoded addresses or credentials, obfuscated or suspicious logic not caught by the static grep rules. Reentrancy on the main ICasinoGameV2 surface is now structurally addressed at the facet layer (nonReentrant guards on value-moving entrypoints; step handlers are view and only ever reached via staticcall, so a game contract cannot reenter through them -- CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md) -- focus reentrancy-style scrutiny on (a) dead/unreachable .call-style code left in the contract (see SEC-04) and (b) any non-ICasinoGameV2 entry points the contract exposes outside the facet's staticcall path.
UI-contract integration correctness: guest's hostApi.openSession/submitAction gameData encoding matches what the contract actually decodes; sessionKey correlation is handled correctly.
manifest capabilities truthfully reflect the contract's actual shape (e.g. submitAction:false for a contract whose onPlayerAction always reverts).

If maxPayout/wager exceeds the heavy-tail multiplier threshold (default 100x) and probabilityWad is under the heavy-tail probability threshold (default 1e15 WAD = 0.1%), the game is heavy-tail per CasinoRiskLib.isHeavyTail. A heavy-tail game that quotes bodyVarianceScaled == 0 CANNOT be whitelisted at all -- hard revert CasinoConfigFacet__HeavyTailGameWithoutVarianceSource -- unless the security council has registered a per-game sigma floor (setGameSigmaFloor). This is a whitelist-blocking defect, not just a mispriced-risk warning; treat it as critical. Also note: the whitelist guard probes quoteRiskParams at each vault's minimum bet using empty gameData unless the council supplies referenceGameData, so a game that reverts on empty/default gameData silently skips this check entirely -- flag that too if seen.

Any mapping from bytes32 randomness (in onRandomness, and any off-chain mirror/mock/test helper) to a small discrete domain (dice faces, card draws, weighted paytable index, tile order) must match RANDOMNESS_DICE.md's canonical algorithm exactly: reject bytes >= floor(256/n)*n (252 for d6) before applying `% n`. Do not reimplement a 'close enough' variant in guest/off-chain code -- it must match the on-chain algorithm exactly, not just be independently unbiased.

quoteForfeitPayout must return 0 for any game whose mid-round value depends on unresolved randomness or hidden state (blackjack-style); a nonzero quote is correct only for a true anytime-cash-out game whose value is fully determined by already-revealed ctx.gameState (mines-style). A concrete nonzero quote on a hidden-state game is an adverse-selection exploit: the player abandons exactly when the real continuation value is below the quote.

hostApi.revealOutcome is invoked exactly once per settled session, after the win-presentation/animation finishes (not eagerly at the instant the session is seen as settled), on every reachable win path including multi-step/bonus-round settlements -- not just the simplest spin. Calling it on a loss is a harmless no-op, so only missing-on-a-win paths matter.

Guest clamps player-facing wager input to the live casino risk limits (equivalent to the SDK's computeMaxWager helper, or an inverted quoteCaps calculation for non-linear payout structures) rather than letting the player submit a wager the facet will bounce with CasinoGameFacet__BetRiskExceedsLimit. Should be rechecked on every snapshot since the limit moves with pool liquidity.

Meta/process note for whoever reads this report, not a submission defect: a clean run in the local Chain SDK simulator is not evidence that quoteRiskParams/bodyVarianceScaled will pass production whitelisting -- the simulator explicitly runs with no diamond, no whitelist governance, and no portfolio risk accounting, so the heavy-tail sigma-floor hard-revert (SEM-12) is invisible there and can only be caught by static/AI review of the actual numbers.
